This edition's own section numbering is NOT sequential within 6 top-level division(s) - genuine gaps in Mueller's own numbering (usually reflecting a stretch with no surviving text at all, not a parsing omission on this importer's part): book-1: jumps from 39 to 41 (no section 40..40 in this edition); book-1: jumps from 56 to 58 (no section 57..57 in this edition); book-2: jumps from 31 to 33 (no section 32..32 in this edition); book-3: jumps from 1 to 3 (no section 2..2 in this edition); book-3: jumps from 9 to 11 (no section 10..10 in this edition); book-3: jumps from 19 to 23 (no section 20..22 in this edition); book-3: jumps from 28 to 32 (no section 29..31 in this edition); book-3: jumps from 34 to 36 (no section 35..35 in this edition); book-3: jumps from 37 to 39 (no section 38..38 in this edition); book-5: jumps from 1 to 3 (no section 2..2 in this edition); book-6: jumps from 4 to 8 (no section 5..7 in this edition); book-fr: jumps from 3 to 5 (no section 4..4 in this edition).

This edition prints NINE top-level divisions, not six: the six traditionally numbered books (1-6) plus three separately-transmitted fragment collections Mueller could not place within a numbered book ("1fr" after Book 1, "3fr" after Book 3, and a final "fr" for fragments not assignable to any particular book). All nine are preserved as separate top-level Divisions, in document order, each with its own verbatim sourceHeading; see about.json.
9 <del> spans (Mueller's apparatus brackets these as probable interpolations, not his judged authentic text) were excluded from the reading text; every occurrence is logged individually above.
11 <add> editorial insertions were kept verbatim in the reading text; every occurrence is logged individually above and flagged on its Passage.

147 <gap reason="lost" .../> markers (manuscript lacunae, from a few missing words up to "34 pages" in a single Book 1 gap) were encountered; 119 carried a literal "rend" rendering (Mueller's own printed dots, e.g. ". . ." or ". . . . ."), kept verbatim, and 28 carried none (nothing was fabricated in their place). Every occurrence is logged individually above with its full reason/extent/rend values.
1 <note> citation gloss(es) embedded mid-quotation (identifying the immediate source of that quotation, not Mueller's own text) were excluded entirely, tag and content.

note: Every fragment section's <bibl> source-citation (e.g. "Non. p. 426M", "Lactant. Div. Inst. 3.16.5") is KEPT as part of the reading text, unlike a Perseus editorial <note> elsewhere in this app. This is a deliberate judgement call: unlike a Perseus-added aside, a Teubner-style "Fragmenta" collection's citation is standard apparatus for how the edition itself presents each fragment on the printed page, and is not really separable from what the "text" of a fragment is. Flagged here explicitly since it is a judgement call, not a certainty - see the importer module doc and the final report.

162 chapter milestones captured; each section's Division.ref is the nearest preceding chapter value within its own top-level division, reset to null at the start of each division (the three fragment collections carry none at all, so every one of their sections has ref=null). This edition also marks 9 <milestone unit="chapter_alt"/> (an alternate numbering, only in Book 6) and 6 <milestone unit="section"/> (marking a shift in which later author's quotation is being followed, e.g. "34(fr1)") - this app's schema has no field for either, so both are dropped as scaffolding without affecting the reading text or Division.ref. Every Passage.ref is null throughout.
